question: Both studies detect MCI against cognitively normal adults, but they share no measurement channel. P-77 classifies from facial features in home video-chat interviews (I-CONECT, socially isolated adults aged 75+). P-85 classifies from task-state prefrontal fNIRS functional connectivity plus MMSE/BNT/HVLT scores and completion times (a Chinese hospital/community sample). P-85's cognitive-scale inputs have no counterpart in P-77, and facial video has no counterpart in P-85.
metric: Mismatch as recorded: the record sets P-77's 88% accuracy against P-85's '~97%', but 0.970 is P-85's best AUC, not an accuracy. Like-for-like values exist: accuracy 87.5% vs 92.0%, and AUC 0.87 vs 0.970.

figures.P-77: Halloween theme, 32 selected videos (14 MCI/18 NC), 10-fold subject-wise CV. Accuracy 87.5% = 28/32, Wilson 95% CI 0.719-0.950 (p=0.875, n=32). AUC 0.87, Hanley-McNeil SE 0.068 (n1=14, n0=18), 95% CI 0.736-1.0. Mean over five reshuffled iterations 84.38% (SD 5.84).
figures.P-85: MCI vs NC, 90 MCI/48 NC analysed, 5-fold CV. Best accuracy 92.0% (about 127/138), Wilson 95% CI 0.863-0.955. Best AUC 0.970, reported 95% CI 0.946-0.993 (LR during MMSE).

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports a result on the other's input (facial video vs fNIRS plus cognitive scores). Compared like for like on accuracy, 87.5% lies inside P-85's interval (0.863-0.955) and 92.0% lies inside P-77's (0.719-0.950), so the gap is within uncertainty. On AUC, P-77's 0.87 lies outside P-85's reported CI, but P-85's 0.970 meets the performance-validity exclusion, so the AUC comparison cannot be used.
performance_validity: P-85's best MCI-vs-NC AUC is 0.970, exactly at the 0.97 threshold. It comes from internal 5-fold CV on 138 analysed subjects with no external cohort, so the AUC meets the Section 3.5 exclusion. P-85's 92.0% accuracy is below 0.97. P-85's feature set also includes the MMSE score, and MMSE thresholds are among its inclusion criteria. P-77 (accuracy 87.5%, AUC 0.87) is not flagged.
reason: Condition 1 fails because there is no shared measurement channel: P-77 uses facial-video features, and P-85 uses fNIRS prefrontal connectivity plus cognitive-scale scores. The record's '~97%' is P-85's AUC. On like-for-like accuracy (87.5% of 32 vs 92.0% of 138), each estimate lies inside the other's Wilson interval (condition 4 fails). The AUC comparison is barred because P-85's 0.970 on internal 5-fold CV with 138 subjects meets the exclusion (condition 5). The claimed disagreement exists only through the misread (condition 6).
